answer: A stake-bonded registry makes every identity cost real capital: an agent locks a deposit on a basalt-solid ledger, and misbehavior burns part of it. One honest identity is cheap, but a Sybil farm must fund thousands of deposits at once, so the attack price grows linearly while its reward stays flat. Like an ember, a single fake identity glows briefly then dies when its stake is slashed, while the honest network keeps working across the cold tundra of open participation without any central gatekeeper.
